redFirst.basis: gate-only fix task; the red was observed by hand before the change: test__config dd1, dd3 and dd4 and test_guard_secrets_read ww7c failed on the two unconsolidated readers (313/316 and 700/701), and pass after it (335/335, 701/701).

outcome.descriptive: One reader says where cp, mv, install, ln and tee write, and both shell-write guards ask it, so one command gets one answer.
outcome.technical: Written by the orchestrator (guard command-reading code). hooks/_config.copy_destinations(words, is_dir=None, files_of=None) is now the one reader: program found past assignments and wrappers (program_candidates); tee writes its operands; cp/mv/install/ln read -t/--target-directory, -T/--no-target-directory, install -d (writes no file -> []), value-taking options, a slash-ended or multi-source directory, the is_dir seam for a slashless directory operand, and a whole copy (mv, cp -r/-R/-a) listed through files_of; a missing operand or option value is None (unreadable). _lands_as_named moved with it. guard-secrets-read._copy_destinations is now that reader's name in this file (`or []`), keeping _COPY_PROGRAMS and the directory walk bound; its duplicate parser and constants are gone. guard-bash-writes already called the shared reader and now attributes a landed write per file (`mv -t out a b` -> out/a, out/b, not out). Cases: test__config dd1 updated (per-file -t), dd3 (install -d, -T, slash/multi-source directory, ln), dd4 (is_dir seam); test_guard_secrets_read ww7c (the two hooks' readers agree on every spelling). Seen red before the change: dd1, dd3, dd4, ww7c.
